title: shipyard CLI manifest
description: A CLI's command and flag grammar, recorded from the running binary by `shipyard gen-cli-manifest`. The manifest asserts what the CLI *documents* in its help output, which is not necessarily everything it accepts. It is a recording, never hand-edited: the generator rewrites it wholesale.

schema.description: URL of this schema, so a consumer can validate without being told where to look.

version.description: Manifest format version. A v2 grammar gets its own schema and its own file.

name.description: The program name, as the CLI prints it in its own usage lines.

summary.description: The CLI's one-line self-description, when its help output opens with one.

engine.description: The parser that produced this manifest, as declared in plugin.yml's cli: block.

usages.description: Invocation forms that take no command word, such as `--version`.

lede.description: Prose a reader needs before the first command. Declared in plugin.yml's `cli:` block, because help output has nowhere to put it.

groups.description: The reference page's sections, in order. Declared in plugin.yml. The generator refuses a group naming a command the CLI doesn't document, and refuses a documented command that no group lists — so this covers every entry in `commands` exactly once.

examples.description: Worked examples keyed by command name, declared in plugin.yml. A command with no entry simply has none.

notes.description: Prose about a command, keyed by command name, declared in plugin.yml. Markdown. Help output gives a one-line summary per form and nothing about why a command refuses or what it stamps, so this is the half of the reference no recording can produce.

commands.description: Commands in the order the CLI documents them. Help order is part of the recording: re-sorting would make every reordering of the help text a no-op diff and every real move invisible.

name.description: The command word verbatim. For a documented alternation (`install|uninstall|status`) this is the raw text and `choices` carries the parsed alternatives.

usages.description: The invocation forms documented for this command. More than one entry means the CLI documents genuinely different forms (`find --url` vs `find --path`), not a formatting artifact.

summary.description: The trailing prose on the usage line, verbatim and unparsed — help text is a lossy source and splitting a description from a parenthetical note would be guessing.

name.description: The placeholder name with its brackets stripped. For an alternation this is the raw text and `choices` carries the alternatives.
The flag as written, long or short.

arg.description: The argument placeholder. Absent means the flag is a boolean switch.

exclusive_with.description: The sibling flags this one is documented as mutually exclusive with. Named rather than numbered so the relation survives a reordering of the group.

flagTrue.description: Present only when true, so the common case stays out of the diff.
